To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Majorana wavefunction in a chain of magnetic adatoms is strongly localized, that the localization length is small compared to the superconducting coherence length, and that the localization is caused by strong renormalization of the Fermi velocity.
the localization of Majorana states is a natural consequence of their strong renormalization of the velocity of quasiparticles.
(i) the Majorana end state in chains of magnetic impurities is strongly localized and (ii) the localization length is parametrically smaller than the bulk coherence length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical description of Majorana states in a linear chain of magnetic impurities.
the physics of quantum impurities on superconducting substrates.
the interplay of superconductivity and magnetic impurities, which is of fundamental interest and also has important implications for the search for Majorana bound state in condensed matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experiment is compatible with the existence of Majorana end states, but it is not yet conclusive proof.
the experiment of Nadj-Perge et al. is not inconsistent with the presence of Majorana states.
the observed end states in the experiment of Nadj-Perge are Majorana bound states, and they are localized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Majorana states are not necessarily localized, but that their localization can be made strong.
Majorana end states are strongly localized on a scale much shorter than the superconducting coherence length.
the localization of Majorana bound states can be understood as a consequence of the strong renormalization of the Fermi velocity in the vicinity of a magnetic impurity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Majorana states in the experiment can be strongly localized without being topological.
the localization length can be made small by tuning the impurity concentration.
Majorana bound states on magnetic impurities can be strongly localized even in a clean superconductor.
